text:
Alex: FYI ran a focused 4h perf scan on the canary cluster after last week's split-queue change. Dropping notes here for runtime + SRE.
Mira: nice, short summary first? :eyes:
Alex: summary: prefill/decode separation cut median end-to-end by ~7%, but decode tail (95p/99p) regressed; root cause looks like KV cache churn during bursty decode batches which increases kernel fallback.
Sam: can you paste the profiler top lines where the tail shows?
Alex: pasted snippet from the perf-trace around a 99p spike:
```
[TRACE] 00:42:11 stage=decode wait=kv_warmup avg=18ms
[TRACE] kernel_pick: fast_quantized -> fallback_generic x 88
[TRACE] batching: decode token_budget=16 -> batch_size jitter [2..9]
[METRICS] kv_hit_rate: baseline 0.80 -> 0.38 during spike
[METRICS] kernel_fallback_rate: 0.9% -> 5.7%
```
Mira: kv_hit_rate dropping that much explains fallback churn. Why is decode causing more unique KV keys?
Zach: my hunch: separating queues increased decode batching granularity, resulting in more short-lived decode batches that touch later offsets (streamed prefixes) across many sessions -> higher key entropy and evictions.
Sam: do we have an access-entropy heatmap per phase?
Alex: yep, uploaded by perf-bot: https://perf.internal/heatmaps/2266001234-phase-entropy (decode shows broader spread vs prefill).
perf-bot: heatmap uploaded for run 2266001234
Mira: action options I see: (A) bump decode token_budget to form larger decode batches, (B) add short-term KV pinning for hot prefixes, (C) dynamic kernel selection to prefer miss-tolerant kernels, (D) prefetch likely keys when burst detected.
Sam: (A) seems lowest-risk to verify. Any data?
Alex: quick canary with token_budget from 16->32: decode avg batch size increased 4.8->9.6, kv_hit_rate 0.38->0.62 during previous spike window, decode 95p down ~14ms. Cost delta +2.6% on GPU time.
Zach: good win. But static larger token_budget wastes cycles when traffic is stable. Suggest adaptive TB with hysteresis: upscale when kv_hit_rate < X for T seconds, downscale when >Y for T2 seconds.
Sam: agree. Prototype controller we ran looked like this:
```
adaptive_decode:
  enabled: true
  hit_rate_low: 0.6
  hit_rate_high: 0.75
  incr: 8
  decr: 8
  min_tb: 8
  max_tb: 64
  up_window_s: 10
  down_window_s: 30
  cooldown_s: 45
```
It used moving average of kv_hit_rate and a cooldown to avoid oscillation. In load tests it converged quickly.
Mira: how did kernel_fallback_rate react?
Alex: fallback_rate dropped from 5.7%->1.3% in the spike windows after adaptive TB engaged. Tail latencies improved accordingly.
Zach: what about prefetcher? We prototyped an async prefetcher that enqueues KV warms for predicted keys when queue_depth>N. But it caused CPU and IO contention on host in the first run. Needs a bounded threadpool and IO throttling.
Sam: if we do adaptive TB + controlled prefetch (offloaded to SRE-managed IO pool) we might get best of both worlds.
Mira: telemetry requirements before rollout: per-route kv_hit_rate, kernel_fallback_rate, decode_p95/p99, token_compute_secs delta, and tb level time series. Also a safe rollback trigger.
Alex: added a small rollback guard: if cost increases >10% for 5m OR decode_p99 doesn't improve after tb increments, auto-disable adaptive on that ring.
Sam: I'll add dashboards and an alert rule in the canary dashboard. ETA EOD.
Zach: I'll run a kernel-selection simulation: prefer fallback_generic only when (batch_size < B AND kv_hit_rate < H) else choose fast_quantized; post results tomorrow. Need to ensure selection decision is cheap and uses recent telemetry.
Alex: note: kernel switches have stateful setup cost in runtime (warmup paths). Frequent switching caused CPU jitter in earlier experiments, so restrict kernel change frequency to >60s per worker.
Mira: ops coordination: SRE, please reserve ~15% CPU headroom on canary hosts for prefetcher trials. I'll ping infra.
Sam: dashboard link (wip): https://dash.internal/canary/adaptive-decode-2266001234 (will update with strand metrics).
perf-bot: canary profile saved: https://perf.internal/runs/2266001234/canary-report
Alex: plan: 1) enable adaptive TB in 10% ring (today), 2) monitor dashboard + rollback guard (Sam), 3) run kernel-selection sim (Zach), 4) prefetcher offload trial with SRE schedule (pending infra).
Mira: timeline and owners?
Alex: Sam - dashboards + rollout guard (EOD). Zach - kernel sim (tomorrow). Alex - enable adaptive TB 10% (2h live then report). Mira - SRE coordination.
Sam: ACK :white_check_mark:
Zach: ACK, will keep kernel switches rate-limited in sim.
Alex: I'll post the 2h metrics back into this thread once the canary finishes. If adaptive TB fixes tail without big cost, we can fold into default and continue kernel work separately.
Mira: thanks all. If tail persists after adaptive rollout, escalate to runtime kernel changes and KV pin heuristics.
Alex: closing thread for now, will update with numbers. Thanks!
